ugadi-significance.description: Ugadi significance explained: the story of Brahma beginning creation, the bitter-sweet pachadi, the panchangam reading, and what a new year asks of us.
outline: Hook: The first thing many Telugu and Kannada families eat on the new year is a spoonful of neem flower. The story says Brahma began creation on this day; the pachadi says the year he made will not be all sweet.

## Ugadi significance: the day time begins again — the tradition, preserved in the Brahma Purana retellings, that creation began on Chaitra Shukla Pratipada; yuga + adi, the start of an age; Gudi Padwa as the same morning in Maharashtra

## Why does the new year start with something bitter? — neem flower, jaggery, tamarind, raw mango, salt and pepper in one spoon; the story is really about agreeing in advance to the whole year, not only the good parts
## Listening to the year: the panchangam reading — panchanga sravanam in temples and homes, the forecast heard with the family, and why the listening matters more than the predictions
Close: eat the bitter part first and slowly; then name one thing you are willing to receive in the coming year, even if it does not taste good.
takeaways: Ugadi marks the lunar new year for Telugu and Kannada families, on the first day of the bright half of Chaitra, traditionally the day Brahma began creation.
Ugadi pachadi mixes six tastes, from bitter neem to sweet jaggery, as a quiet promise to accept the whole year, not just its pleasant days.
The panchangam reading on Ugadi is less about prediction than about a family sitting together to hear the year begin.

faq.q: When is Ugadi celebrated?
faq.a: Ugadi falls on the first day of the bright half of the lunar month of Chaitra, the day after the new moon, which usually lands in March or April. Because it follows the lunar calendar, the date moves each year. Check the current year's panchangam or your local temple's calendar for the exact day and the auspicious time for the morning puja.

faq.q: Why is Ugadi celebrated?
faq.a: Ugadi is celebrated as the start of a new lunar year. Tradition holds that Brahma began creating the world on this day, so it is treated as a fresh beginning for the household. Families clean the home, hang mango-leaf torans, wear new clothes, pray, eat the six-taste Ugadi pachadi and listen to the new year's panchangam being read aloud.

faq.q: What is the story of Brahma and Ugadi?
faq.a: The ugadi story most families tell is that Brahma, the creator, began the work of creation on the first day of Chaitra, which is why time is counted afresh from this morning. The name itself joins yuga, an age, and adi, a beginning. The story frames the new year as creation starting again, with the household invited to begin with it.

faq.q: Is Ugadi the same as Gudi Padwa?
faq.a: They fall on the same day and share the idea of a lunar new year. Ugadi is the Telugu and Kannada name; Gudi Padwa is the Marathi celebration, where families raise a gudi, a decorated pole topped with an upturned pot, at the doorway. Customs and foods differ by region, but the meaning of a fresh start is common to both.

puthandu-tamil-new-year-usa.description: Tamil New Year Puthandu in the USA: keeping Chithirai's first morning on a workday, the fruit tray at dawn, mango pachadi, and calling home across time zones.
outline: Hook: In Chennai my mother has already cooked the maanga pachadi by the time my alarm goes off in New Jersey; Puthandu arrives at home before it arrives here.

## When is Tamil New Year Puthandu, and why doesn't it move much? — a solar new year: the first day of Chithirai, when the sun enters Mesha, usually in mid-April; unlike Ugadi it follows the sun, so the date stays close each year; check the panchangam for the exact day

## The morning at home, even on a Tuesday — the tray set the night before (fruits, a mirror, a little gold, flowers, betel), seeing it first at dawn, a kolam at the door, a lamp, a sweet-and-sour mango pachadi and vadai if there is time

## Calling India, finding a temple, telling the kids — the time difference (India's evening is our morning), temples holding the panchangam reading on the nearest weekend, and a two-line version of the story for an eleven-year-old
Close: the Tirukkural opens with the first letter of the alphabet; this week, begin something small on Puthandu morning, even if it is only the lamp before the laptop.
takeaways: Tamil New Year, Puthandu, falls on the first day of Chithirai, when the sun enters Mesha, usually in mid-April, so it stays close to the same date each year.
In the USA, families keep it by setting a fruit tray to see at dawn, lighting a lamp, cooking mango pachadi and calling home before India's evening ends.

faq.q: When is Tamil New Year celebrated?
faq.a: Puthandu, the Tamil New Year, falls on the first day of the solar month of Chithirai, when the sun moves into Mesha, the sign of Aries in the sidereal zodiac. That usually happens in mid-April. Because it follows the sun rather than the moon, the date shifts very little. Check the current year's panchangam for the exact day and time of the transition.

faq.q: How do you do Puthandu celebration at home?
faq.a: The night before, arrange a tray with fruits, flowers, betel leaves, a mirror and a piece of gold or a coin. In the morning, look at it first, then bathe, draw a kolam, light the lamp and pray. Many families cook mango pachadi, which is sweet, sour and bitter at once, along with vadai and payasam, and visit a temple.

faq.q: How can Tamil families celebrate Tamil New Year in America when it falls on a weekday?
faq.a: Keep the dawn part short: see the tray, light the lamp and say a prayer before work. Cook the pachadi in the evening or on the weekend. Call family in India early, because their day is ending as yours begins. Many US temples hold the panchangam reading and special pujas on the nearest weekend, which gives children a community to share it with.

faq.q: Is Puthandu the same as Vishu or Ugadi?
faq.a: Puthandu and Vishu are both solar new years and usually fall on the same day, one in Tamil Nadu and one in Kerala, with different customs. Ugadi is a lunar new year kept by Telugu and Kannada families, on the first day of the bright half of Chaitra, so it often comes a few weeks earlier.

vishu-kani-meaning.description: Vishu kani meaning: why Kerala families arrange rice, konna flowers, gold and a mirror before Krishna, and why the first sight of the year is chosen with care.
outline: Hook: A friend from Kerala told me that on Vishu morning her grandmother covered her eyes with both hands and walked her to the puja room. The first thing she saw that year was chosen for her, with love.
## What is Vishu kani meaning, really? — kani means the first sight; the belief that what you see first on the first day of Medam colours the year; the idea underneath: we can arrange what we let in

## What goes into the urali? — the bell-metal urali with raw rice, golden konna flowers, a kani vellari cucumber, coconut, jackfruit and mango, gold, a val kannadi mirror, a lit nilavilakku, and Krishna at the centre
## Kaineettam, sadya and the rest of the day — elders giving coins to the young, firecrackers, the Vishu sadya; when it falls (the first of Medam, usually mid-April, the same day as Puthandu)
Close: Tirumoolar wrote that the heart is a temple; this week, choose the first thing you look at each morning before the phone does it for you.
takeaways: Vishu kani means the first sight of the new year: an arrangement of rice, konna flowers, fruit, gold, a mirror and a lamp before Krishna, seen at dawn with closed eyes opened.
The custom rests on a simple idea: what you see first on Vishu shapes the year, so you arrange abundance and light for your family to see.

faq.q: How do you arrange Vishu kani?
faq.a: The night before, fill a bell-metal urali with raw rice and arrange konna flowers, a golden cucumber, coconut halves, mango, jackfruit, betel leaves, a gold ornament or coins, a mirror and a folded mundu. Place a picture of Krishna behind it and a nilavilakku lamp beside it. Before dawn, one person lights the lamp and leads the family in, eyes covered.

faq.q: What are the items in the vishu kani list?
faq.a: A typical vishu kani list has an urali, raw rice, konna flowers from the golden shower tree, a kani vellari cucumber, a coconut, mango and jackfruit, betel leaves and areca nut, gold, a val kannadi mirror, a cotton mundu, a nilavilakku with wicks, and an image of Krishna. Families add or leave out items by custom; the idea is abundance and light.

faq.q: What is vishu kaineettam?
faq.a: Vishu kaineettam is the gift of coins or notes that elders give to children and younger family members on Vishu morning, usually right after the kani. It is a small blessing for prosperity in the coming year. In families abroad, grandparents often send it by video call and a parent hands over the coin on their behalf.

faq.q: When is Vishu celebrated?
faq.a: Vishu falls on the first day of the Malayalam month of Medam, when the sun enters Mesha, which usually comes in mid-April, on or near the same day as Tamil New Year. Because it follows the solar calendar, it moves very little. Check the current year's panchangam for the exact day, since the transition time decides it.

ram-navami-puja-at-home.description: Ram Navami puja at home, step by step: a simple noon ritual with a lamp, tulsi, panakam and a reading of Rama's birth, adapted for a US workday or lunch break.
secondaryKeywords: why ram navami is celebrated at noon
outline: Hook: Rama is said to have been born at midday. So this is a festival you can keep in a lunch hour: twenty minutes, a lamp and a glass of panakam.

## Why is Ram Navami celebrated at noon? — the Valmiki Ramayana's Bala Kanda places Rama's birth on the ninth day of the bright half of Chaitra, in Punarvasu, at midday; the madhyahna hour as the heart of the puja

## Ram Navami puja at home in six steps — clean the space, a picture of Rama with Sita, Lakshmana and Hanuman, lamp and flowers, a short sankalpam, tulsi leaves offered one by one while chanting 'Sri Rama Jayam', aarti
## Panakam, neer mor and a reading — jaggery water with dry ginger and cardamom, spiced buttermilk, kosambari; reading the birth chapter or a few verses of the Ram Raksha Stotra aloud
Close: try this for a week after the festival: chant Rama's name eleven times at noon, wherever you are, and notice what happens to the afternoon.
takeaways: Ram Navami puja at home is traditionally done around noon, the hour of Rama's birth, with a lamp, tulsi leaves, flowers, panakam and a short reading.
On a US workday, a twenty-minute midday puja, or an evening one with the same steps, keeps the festival without needing a priest.

faq.q: What is the simple ram navami puja vidhi at home?
faq.a: Clean your puja space and set up a picture of Rama with Sita, Lakshmana and Hanuman. Light a lamp, offer flowers and tulsi, and state your sankalpam, a short statement of intention. Chant Rama's name or a stotra, offer panakam, neer mor and fruit as naivedyam, wave a camphor or ghee lamp for aarti, and share the offering with the family.

faq.q: Why is Ram Navami celebrated at noon?
faq.a: The Valmiki Ramayana describes Rama's birth on the ninth day of the bright half of Chaitra, in the star Punarvasu, around midday. So the main puja is traditionally done in the madhyahna, the middle part of the day. Many temples time their abhishekam and birth celebration for noon; if you cannot, an evening puja at home is fine.

faq.q: How can I keep Ram Navami on a weekday in the US?
faq.a: Keep the full puja short and do it at lunch if you work from home, or in the morning before you leave. Make panakam the night before. If the timing does not work, do the puja in the evening with the family. Many temples in the US hold Rama Navami celebrations and Sita Rama kalyanam on the nearest weekend.

faq.q: When is Ram Navami celebrated?
faq.a: Ram Navami falls on the ninth day, navami, of the bright half of the lunar month Chaitra, usually in March or April, about nine days after Ugadi and Gudi Padwa. Some families keep all nine days as Rama Navaratri. The date changes each year, so check the current year's panchangam for the day and midday timing.

hanuman-jayanti-significance.description: Hanuman Jayanti significance: why regional dates differ, what the stories of the leap and the forgotten strength mean, and how families honour Hanuman at home.
secondaryKeywords: hanuman jayanti date in tamil nadu
outline: Hook: As a child, the story goes, Hanuman saw the rising sun and leapt for it, thinking it was a ripe fruit. The story is about a boy with too much strength; the festival is about what happens when strength learns to serve.

## Why is Hanuman Jayanti on different days? — Chaitra Purnima in much of North India; the new moon of Margazhi in Mula star in Tamil Nadu; a longer observance ending in Vaishakha in Telugu homes; the same devotion, several calendars

## The strength he forgot — the curse of the sages that made him forget his powers, and Jambavan reminding him on the shore in the Kishkindha Kanda; the story is really about how often we need someone else to tell us what we can do

## Hanuman Jayanti significance in the home — vadai malai and betel leaf garlands in the South, sindoor and laddoos in the North, the Hanuman Chalisa or Sundara Kanda read aloud; strength offered, not displayed
Close: a gentle reframe: the strongest figure in the Ramayana spends the whole epic as someone's messenger. Ask whom your strength is working for.
takeaways: Hanuman Jayanti celebrates Hanuman's birth, but the day differs by region: Chaitra Purnima in the North, the new moon of Margazhi in Tamil Nadu, and other dates elsewhere.
Its significance is strength in service: Hanuman's power is remembered not for itself but for what he did for Rama and Sita.

faq.q: Why is Hanuman Jayanti celebrated on different dates?
faq.a: Regional calendars mark Hanuman's birth differently. Much of North India observes it on the full moon of Chaitra, in March or April. Tamil Nadu observes Hanumath Jayanthi on the new moon of Margazhi, in December or January, when it coincides with Mula star. Telugu and Kannada traditions keep other dates. Follow your family's custom and check the local panchangam.

faq.q: What is the story of Hanuman forgetting his powers?
faq.a: In the Ramayana tradition, young Hanuman's pranks disturbed sages in the forest, who laid a curse that he would forget his strength until someone reminded him. In the Kishkindha Kanda, as the monkeys despair on the shore facing the ocean, the old bear Jambavan recounts Hanuman's birth and power. Remembering, Hanuman grows and leaps across the sea to Lanka.

faq.q: Why is Hanuman Jayanti celebrated?
faq.a: Families celebrate Hanuman Jayanti to honour Hanuman's birth and the qualities he stands for: courage, loyalty, humility and tireless service to Rama. Devotees visit temples, offer vadai garlands, betel leaves, butter or sindoor depending on region, and read the Hanuman Chalisa or Sundara Kanda. Many see it as a day to ask for steadiness rather than spectacle.

akshaya-tritiya-significance.description: Akshaya Tritiya significance: the stories of Sudama's rice, the Akshaya Patra and Parashurama, and why giving, not only buying gold, is the heart of the day.
secondaryKeywords: what to donate on akshaya tritiya
outline: Hook: A poor Brahmin walks to Dwaraka with a handful of beaten rice tied in a cloth, too ashamed to offer it. Krishna eats it with joy. The story is about a gift so small it was nearly hidden, and a day named for what never runs out.

## Akshaya Tritiya significance: what 'akshaya' means — the third day of the bright half of Vaishakha, usually April or May; akshaya as that which does not diminish; the belief that what you begin or give today keeps growing

## Which stories belong to this day? — Sudama and the aval; the Akshaya Patra given to the Pandavas in exile so no guest went hungry; Parashurama's birth; the tradition that Vyasa began dictating the Mahabharata to Ganesha

## Gold, or giving? — how buying gold became the modern custom; the older practice of dana: water pots, fans, umbrellas and food in the summer heat; the story is really about the vessel, not what it holds
Close: the Akshaya Patra fed everyone until Draupadi herself had eaten; on this day, feed someone before you buy anything.
takeaways: Akshaya Tritiya falls on the third day of the bright half of Vaishakha; akshaya means never diminishing, and the day is believed to make good beginnings and gifts last.
Its oldest stories, Sudama's beaten rice and the Pandavas' Akshaya Patra, are about generosity and food, not gold.

faq.q: Why is Akshaya Tritiya celebrated?
faq.a: Akshaya Tritiya is celebrated as a day when good actions are believed to bear lasting fruit, since akshaya means that which does not diminish. It is linked with Parashurama's birth, Krishna receiving Sudama's beaten rice, and the Akshaya Patra that fed the Pandavas. Families pray to Lakshmi and Vishnu, start new ventures, and give food, water and clothing.

faq.q: What is the Akshaya Tritiya story?
faq.a: Several stories gather around the day. The best known is Sudama, Krishna's poor childhood friend, who brought only a handful of beaten rice to Dwaraka; Krishna received it gladly and Sudama returned home to find his family provided for. Another tells of the sun god giving the exiled Pandavas the Akshaya Patra, a vessel that never ran empty.

faq.q: What to donate on Akshaya Tritiya?
faq.a: Traditional gifts suit the summer season: water in clay pots, buttermilk, fans, umbrellas, footwear, grains, fruit and cooked food. Feeding people, known as annadanam, is considered especially meaningful. Many families also give to a temple or a food programme in their parents' names. Give what you can with a glad heart; the tradition values intention over the size of the gift.

faq.q: Is buying gold on Akshaya Tritiya necessary?
faq.a: No. Buying gold is a popular modern custom built on the idea that what you acquire today keeps growing. The older emphasis of the day is on dana, giving, and on beginning good work. If you do buy something, many families offer it before the lamp first. Nothing is lost by choosing to give instead of buy.

outline: Hook: My son asked once whether gods have birthdays. I told him Murugan's falls in Vaikasi, on the day of the star Visakam, and that we could make him payasam. He was satisfied.

## What is Vaikasi Visakam? — the day the moon is in Visakam in the Tamil month of Vaikasi, usually May or June; the Kanda Puranam story of six sparks from Shiva's third eye, carried to the Saravana pond, raised by the six Krittika mothers and gathered by Parvati into one child with six faces

## Vaikasi Visakam at home, in a small kitchen — a picture or vel, milk or panchamrutham poured slowly, red flowers, a lamp, the Kanda Sashti Kavasam or a few lines of Arunagirinathar's Thiruppugazh, payasam as naivedyam

## Where is the nearest Murugan temple? — US temples with Murugan shrines, calling ahead for the abhishekam time, the weekday problem, taking part in Palani's worship from afar through family or an online sankalpam
Close: Arunagirinathar's Thiruppugazh is full of calls to Murugan by name; this week, say his name once each morning on the way to work.
takeaways: Vaikasi Visakam is Murugan's birthday, observed when the moon is in the star Visakam during the Tamil month of Vaikasi, usually in May or June.
At home, a lamp, a slow milk abhishekam to a vel or picture, red flowers, payasam and a verse from the Kanda Sashti Kavasam are enough.

faq.q: What is the significance of Vaikasi Visakam?
faq.a: Vaikasi Visakam significance comes from the Kanda Puranam: Murugan was born when six sparks from Shiva's third eye fell into the Saravana pond and became six infants, raised by the Krittika maidens and joined by Parvati into one child with six faces. The day celebrates his birth and his role as the one who removes confusion and fear.

faq.q: How do I do Vaikasi Visakam pooja at home?
faq.a: Clean the puja space and place a picture of Murugan or a small vel. Light a lamp, then pour milk, or panchamrutham, slowly over the vel as abhishekam while chanting 'Om Saravanabhava'. Wipe it, offer red flowers and sandal paste, recite the Kanda Sashti Kavasam if you can, and offer payasam or fruit before sharing it with the family.

faq.q: When is Vaikasi Visakam celebrated?
faq.a: It falls on the day the moon is in Visakam star during the Tamil month of Vaikasi, which runs from mid-May to mid-June, and it often coincides with the full moon. The exact day moves each year, so check the current year's panchangam. Murugan temples in India and the US hold special abhishekams and processions.

chitra-pournami-meaning.description: Chitra Pournami, the full moon of Chithirai, and Chitragupta the record-keeper: the story, the moonlit variety-rice meal, and a practice of honest self-review.
outline: Hook: One night a year, tradition says, the keeper of everyone's accounts has a festival of his own. You might use it to keep your own accounts first.

## What is Chitra Pournami? — the full moon of the Tamil month Chithirai, usually April or May, when the moon is near Chitra star; the brightest night of early summer; girivalam at Tiruvannamalai and the Chithirai festival in Madurai

## Who is Chitragupta, and why does he keep a ledger? — the assistant of Yama who records each person's deeds; the legend of his birth from a drawing, hence 'chitra'; his shrine at Kanchipuram; a record-keeper, not a punisher

## Chitra Pournami at home: moonlight, rice and a review — cooking chitrannam, the variety rices (lemon, tamarind, coconut, curd), eating outdoors under the moon, a lamp, and ten minutes looking honestly at your own ledger
Close: try this for a week from the full moon: each night, before sleep, name one thing you did well and one you would redo. That is the whole practice.
takeaways: Chitra Pournami is the full moon of the Tamil month Chithirai, dedicated in tradition to Chitragupta, who records every person's deeds for Yama.
Families cook variety rices and eat under the moon; the quieter practice is to review your own actions honestly, without fear or guilt.

faq.q: What is the significance of Chitra Pournami?
faq.a: Chitra Pournami significance lies in two things: it is one of the brightest full moons of the year, and it is dedicated to Chitragupta, the keeper of records of every person's good and bad actions. Devotees pray to him for clarity, give food, walk around Arunachala at Tiruvannamalai, and in many homes share a moonlit meal of variety rice.

faq.q: Who is Chitragupta?
faq.a: Chitragupta is the divine accountant who serves Yama, recording each person's deeds. One popular legend says he was created from a picture, a chitra, drawn and brought to life, which is how he got his name. He is honoured especially on Chitra Pournami, and a well-known shrine to him stands in Kanchipuram. Tradition sees him as fair, not fearsome.

faq.q: How do I do Chitra Pournami pooja at home?
faq.a: In the evening, clean the puja space, light a lamp and offer flowers to Chitragupta or to your family deity. Cook chitrannam or a few variety rices, offer them, and eat together outdoors or by a window where you can see the full moon. Some families also place a pen and palm-leaf, or a notebook, before the lamp.

faq.q: When is Chitra Pournami?
faq.a: Chitra Pournami falls on the full moon of the Tamil month Chithirai, which runs from mid-April to mid-May, so it usually comes in late April or May. It is the same full moon that anchors the Chithirai festival in Madurai. The exact date changes each year; check the current year's panchangam.

meenakshi-thirukalyanam-festival.description: Meenakshi Thirukalyanam, the divine wedding at the heart of Madurai's Chithirai festival: the story, the thread women renew, and how to join it from far away.
outline: Hook: My uncle in Madurai says the whole city gets dressed for one wedding each year, and that on the morning of the Thirukalyanam you can tell the married women on the bus by the fresh yellow thread at their necks.

## What is Meenakshi Thirukalyanam? — the celestial wedding of Meenakshi and Sundareswarar at the centre of the Chithirai festival, in the Tamil month of Chithirai (April or May); the Thiruvilaiyadal Puranam story of the Pandya princess who ruled, conquered, and met her match on Mount Kailash

## Why does Alagar arrive late? — the story of Meenakshi's brother Kallazhagar setting out from Alagar Kovil to give her away, hearing the wedding is over, and turning back at the Vaigai; what a crowd on a riverbank teaches about showing up anyway

## Keeping the wedding at home — married women renewing the thali thread or manjal kayiru on the day, a lamp and flowers for Meenakshi, watching the temple's live broadcast with parents in India, a small sweet for the family
Close: Manikkavasagar sang of Shiva as the one who came to Madurai for his devotees; this week, go to someone's celebration, even late, even for ten minutes.
takeaways: Meenakshi Thirukalyanam is the divine wedding of Meenakshi and Sundareswarar, the high point of Madurai's Chithirai festival in April or May.
Many married women renew their thali thread on the wedding day, and families far away keep it with a lamp, flowers and the temple broadcast.

faq.q: What is the Chithirai festival in Madurai?
faq.a: The Chithirai festival is Madurai's great spring festival, held over roughly two weeks in the Tamil month of Chithirai. It includes Meenakshi's coronation as queen, her victory procession, the Thirukalyanam or divine wedding with Sundareswarar, a chariot festival, and Kallazhagar's journey from Alagar Kovil to the Vaigai river. It brings together Shaiva and Vaishnava devotion in one city celebration.

faq.q: What is the Meenakshi kalyanam story?
faq.a: The Thiruvilaiyadal Puranam tells of Meenakshi, born to the Pandya king of Madurai, raised as heir and crowned queen. She led her armies to the north and conquered every land until she reached Kailash and saw Shiva, when she recognised him as her husband. Shiva came to Madurai as Sundareswarar, and their wedding is re-enacted every Chithirai.

faq.q: Why does Alagar enter the Vaigai river?
faq.a: In the festival story, Kallazhagar, a form of Vishnu and Meenakshi's brother, sets out from Alagar Kovil to give his sister away. By the time he reaches the Vaigai, the wedding is over, so he enters the river, blesses the devotees and returns. The event, usually near Chitra Pournami, draws enormous crowds to the riverbanks.

faq.q: Can I take part in Meenakshi Thirukalyanam from abroad?
faq.a: Yes. The wedding is widely broadcast, and many families watch it together across time zones, often late at night in the US. At home, light a lamp, offer flowers and a sweet to Meenakshi and Sundareswarar, and married women may renew their thali thread. You can also have an archana done at the temple in your family's names.

outline: Hook: In the Tamil month of Aadi, loudspeakers at Amman temples play from dawn and pots of ragi koozh are carried through the streets. It is also the month in which families refuse to fix weddings. The story of why tells you what the month is for.

## What gives Aadi month significance? — the Tamil month from mid-July to mid-August, the sun entering Karka and the start of Dakshinayana, the monsoon wind; the season when the Goddess is said to come closest to the village

## Why do families avoid weddings in Aadi? — the practical and the symbolic: planting season, the tradition of new brides returning to their mothers' homes, and the idea that this month's devotion belongs to the Goddess, not to household beginnings; explanations vary by family

## Fridays, Pooram, Amavasya and Perukku — Aadi Velli pujas to Amman, Aadi Pooram as Andal's birth star and the Goddess's valaikappu with bangles, Aadi Amavasya for the ancestors, Aadi Perukku for the river
Close: the story is really about attention: a month when the calendar sets aside our own plans and turns us toward the Mother. Keep one Friday lamp for her.
takeaways: Aadi, the Tamil month from mid-July to mid-August, is dedicated to the Goddess, with Aadi Fridays, Aadi Pooram, Aadi Amavasya and Aadi Perukku.
Families traditionally avoid weddings and housewarmings in Aadi, a custom explained by farming, monsoon and devotion, not by anything to fear.

faq.q: Why is Aadi month not auspicious for marriage?
faq.a: Tamil families traditionally avoid weddings and housewarmings in Aadi for a mix of reasons. It was the busy sowing season, the monsoon winds made travel hard, and newly married brides customarily spent Aadi at their parents' homes. Many also see the month as reserved for the Goddess rather than household beginnings. It is a custom of timing, not a bad omen.

faq.q: How is Aadi velli pooja done?
faq.a: On each Friday of Aadi, women clean the home, draw a kolam, and light a lamp for the Goddess, often Lakshmi or the local Amman. They offer flowers, turmeric, kumkum and a sweet, and may recite Lalitha Sahasranamam or Abhirami Anthathi. Many visit an Amman temple, offer koozh, or give bangles and turmeric to married women as thamboolam.

faq.q: What is the significance of Aadi Pooram?
faq.a: Aadi Pooram falls on the day of Pooram star in Aadi and is celebrated as the birth of Andal, the poet-saint of Srivilliputhur, and as a festival of the Goddess. In many Amman temples, the Goddess receives a valaikappu, an offering of bangles like a baby shower, and devotees take the bangles home as prasadam for fertility and family well-being.

aadi-perukku-meaning.description: Aadi Perukku, the eighteenth day of Aadi when the Kaveri rises: offerings to the river, the variety rices, the yellow thread, and keeping it far from home.
outline: Hook: Thatha used to close the cloth shop in Kumbakonam early on Aadi Perukku, because nobody bought saris that afternoon; everyone was at the Kaveri with a bundle of variety rice.

## What is Aadi Perukku? — the eighteenth day of the Tamil month of Aadi, usually early August, when the monsoon swells the Kaveri; perukku means rising; the day the delta thanks the river that feeds it

## At the river: rice, thread and lamps — women offering turmeric, flowers and lamps to the water; chitrannam, the lemon, tamarind, coconut and curd rices; newlyweds and married women tying fresh yellow thread; Srirangam's gifts sent to the Kaveri as to a sister

## How do you keep Aadi Perukku far from the Kaveri? — a bowl of water with turmeric and flowers on the balcony, a small lamp, a variety rice lunch, a video call to someone who can see the river, and a walk to whatever water is near you
Close: an old Tamil saying attributed to Avvaiyar holds that a town without a river has no beauty; this week, find out where your own water comes from and say thank you to it once.
takeaways: Aadi Perukku falls on the eighteenth day of the Tamil month of Aadi, when families thank the rising Kaveri and other rivers with lamps, flowers, rice and turmeric.
Away from the Kaveri, a bowl of water with turmeric and flowers, a lamp and a variety rice meal keep the gratitude of the day.

faq.q: What is the significance of Aadi Perukku?
faq.a: Aadi Perukku significance is gratitude to water. It falls when the monsoon has filled the Kaveri and other Tamil Nadu rivers just before the sowing season. Families, especially women, go to the riverbank to offer lamps, flowers, turmeric and rice to the river as a mother and a goddess, and pray for a good harvest and a steady household.

faq.q: Why is it called the Aadi 18 festival?
faq.a: Aadi Perukku is also called Padinettam Perukku, the rising of the eighteenth, because it falls on the eighteenth day of the Tamil solar month of Aadi, which usually corresponds to early August. The number is tied to the solar calendar, so the day stays fairly steady each year. Check the panchangam for the exact date.

faq.q: How do I do Aadi Perukku pooja at home?
faq.a: Fill a brass or steel vessel with water, add turmeric, a few flowers and a coin, and place it near your puja space or on a balcony. Light a lamp beside it, offer a variety rice such as lemon or coconut rice, and say a short prayer of thanks for water. Married women may tie a fresh turmeric thread.

## Varalakshmi vratham pooja at home: the kalasam — a silver or brass pot filled with water or rice, a coconut smeared with turmeric, mango leaves, a Lakshmi face or picture, a blouse piece and jewellery; set up the night before

## What is the Charumathi story? — the tale, told by Shiva to Parvati in the tradition, of a devoted woman to whom Lakshmi appeared in a dream and asked for this Friday's worship; the vratham as gratitude, not a transaction

## A workday version that still counts — morning lamp and sankalpam, tying the nombu charadu yellow thread on the right wrist, a short Lakshmi Ashtottaram, naivedyam of fruit and a sweet; evening aarti and thamboolam for friends
Close: try this: whatever the weekday, give your full attention to one ten-minute window of the puja. Lakshmi, the tradition says, stays where she is noticed.
takeaways: Varalakshmi Vratham is kept on the Friday before the full moon of Shravana, usually July or August, with a decorated kalasam as Lakshmi and a yellow thread tied on the wrist.
On a workday, do the kalasam, sankalpam and thread in the morning and the aarti and thamboolam in the evening; no priest is needed.

faq.q: How do you do varalakshmi vratham kalasam decoration?
faq.a: Fill a brass or silver kalasam with water, raw rice or coins, and add betel leaves, a few mango leaves and a turmeric-smeared coconut on top. Tie a blouse piece or small cloth around the neck of the pot, place a Lakshmi face or picture against the coconut, and add jewellery, flowers and a garland. Set it on a plate of rice.

faq.q: What is the Varalakshmi Vratham story?
faq.a: The traditional story, told by Shiva to Parvati, is about Charumathi, a devoted wife and daughter-in-law. Lakshmi appeared to her in a dream and asked her to worship Varalakshmi, the Lakshmi who grants boons, on the Friday before Shravana's full moon. Charumathi and the women of her town did so, and their homes were blessed with well-being.

faq.q: Can I do Varalakshmi pooja on a working day?
faq.a: Yes. Many women in the US split the puja: set up the kalasam the night before, then in the morning light the lamp, make the sankalpam, tie the yellow thread and offer fruit and a sweet. In the evening, do the aarti, read or play the story, and give thamboolam to friends. A focused shorter puja is completely acceptable.

faq.q: When is Varalakshmi Vratham?
faq.a: Varalakshmi Vratham falls on the Friday before the full moon of the lunar month Shravana, which usually lands in July or August, in the Tamil months of Aadi or Avani. If that Friday is not possible, some families observe it on a following Friday of the month. Check the current year's panchangam for the date.

avani-avittam-meaning.description: Avani Avittam, the day of changing the sacred thread: what upakarma renews, why Hayagriva is remembered on the same full moon, and what it offers any student.
outline: Hook: Every year in Chennai, the morning after the rains, lines of men sat at the temple tank in new white dhotis, changing their threads together. I did not understand it then. I think I understand it now, watching my son start a new school year in New Jersey.

## What is Avani Avittam? — upakarma, the annual renewal of the Vedic student's vow, kept on the full moon of Shravana when the moon is in Avittam in the Tamil month of Avani, usually August; the day varies for Rig, Yajur and Sama Veda families

## Why change the sacred thread? — the yagnopavitam, or poonal, as a vow worn on the body; the old thread set aside, the new one worn with mantras, the Kamo'karshit japa asking pardon for lapses, and the next day's Gayatri japam

## Hayagriva and the return of knowledge — the same full moon as Hayagriva Jayanti, when Vishnu as the horse-headed one restores the stolen Vedas; the day as a festival of learning, not only of a thread
Close: the Taittiriya Upanishad tells the student not to neglect study; this week, pick up one thing you stopped learning and give it fifteen minutes.
takeaways: Avani Avittam is upakarma, the yearly renewal of Vedic study, when those who wear the sacred thread change it with mantras on the full moon of Shravana, usually August.
It shares its full moon with Hayagriva Jayanti, so the day is also a festival of learning and a fresh start for students.

faq.q: What is the significance of Avani Avittam?
faq.a: Avani Avittam significance lies in renewal. It is the day of upakarma, when those initiated into Vedic study renew their commitment, change their sacred thread, and ask forgiveness for lapses over the past year. Traditionally it also marked the start of the Vedic study term. Many families see it as a reminder that learning must be taken up again and again.

faq.q: What does upakarma mean?
faq.a: Upakarma means a beginning or an undertaking, the ceremony that opens a new term of Vedic study. It includes offerings to the rishis who heard the Vedas, the Kamo'karshit japa asking pardon for faults, and wearing a new sacred thread. Different Vedic branches observe it on different days, so Sama Veda families keep it later than Rig and Yajur.

faq.q: How is the poonal changed on Avani Avittam?
faq.a: Changing poonal on Avani Avittam is done after a bath, usually led by a priest or elder at home or at a temple. Participants do sandhyavandanam and sankalpam, offer to the rishis, then wear the new yagnopavitam with its mantra and remove the old one, which is placed in water or under a tree. The next day, many chant the Gayatri mantra over a thousand times.

outline: Hook: King Janamejaya lit a fire to burn every snake in the world, and a boy named Astika talked him out of it. The story says the snakes were saved on a panchami; the story is really about a king learning that grief is not a reason to destroy.

## What is Naga Panchami significance? — the fifth day of the bright half of Shravana, usually July or August, when the rains drive snakes out of their holes; honouring what we fear instead of killing it; regional variants like Nagula Chavithi and Naga Chathurthi

## Why are snakes worshipped in Hinduism? — Shesha beneath Vishnu, Vasuki around Shiva's neck and around Mount Mandara, Kaliya subdued but spared by Krishna; the snake as time, the earth's hidden water, and the coiled energy of the body

## Anthills, stone nagas and milk — women offering turmeric, flowers and milk at anthills and nagakal stones under peepal trees; why the offering goes to the stone, not a live snake, and why many now pour milk only symbolically
Close: in almost every one of these stories, the snake is spared. Perhaps that is the festival's quiet instruction: leave the frightening thing alive, and learn to live beside it.
takeaways: Naga Panchami falls on the fifth day of the bright half of Shravana, when families honour snakes with turmeric, flowers and symbolic milk at anthills and stone nagas.
In the stories, from Kaliya to Astika's rescue, snakes are subdued or spared, never exterminated; the festival teaches coexistence with what we fear.

faq.q: Why do we celebrate Naga Panchami?
faq.a: We celebrate Naga Panchami to honour snakes, who appear often during the monsoon and play a role in keeping fields free of pests. Tradition links the day with Astika saving the serpents from Janamejaya's sacrifice and with Krishna sparing Kaliya. Families pray at anthills and naga stones for the protection of children and the household, and to make peace with fear.

faq.q: What is the Naga Panchami story?
faq.a: The best-known story comes from the Mahabharata. King Janamejaya, grieving his father Parikshit's death from Takshaka's bite, performed a sacrifice to destroy all snakes. The young sage Astika, himself half naga, came to the ritual and persuaded the king to stop. The snakes were spared, and tradition marks that mercy on Naga Panchami.

faq.q: Why are snakes worshipped in Hinduism?
faq.a: Snakes appear throughout Hindu stories: Shesha supports Vishnu, Vasuki coils around Shiva's neck, and nagas guard water and treasure beneath the earth. They are associated with fertility, the monsoon, time and renewal, because they shed their skin. Worship is usually offered to stone images of nagas or at anthills; live snakes are left alone.

takeaways: To keep Krishna Janmashtami at home, draw small footprints to the puja corner, set up a cradle, fast lightly, and offer butter and aval at the midnight hour of his birth.

faq.q: How do I do janmashtami puja at home simple?
faq.a: Clean the puja space and set up a small cradle with a picture or image of baby Krishna. Light a lamp and offer tulsi, flowers, butter, aval, milk sweets and fruit. Chant 'Om Namo Bhagavate Vasudevaya' or sing a bhajan, read the birth story, and at the chosen hour rock the cradle, do aarti, and share the offerings.

faq.q: Why are Krishna's footprints drawn for Gokulashtami?
faq.a: In many South Indian homes, gokulashtami Krishna footprints are drawn with rice flour paste from the front door to the puja room, small and baby-sized. They show little Krishna walking into the house to steal butter and bless the family. Children love making them by pressing the side of a closed fist into the paste and adding toes with a fingertip.

faq.q: What is the Janmashtami midnight puja time in the USA?
faq.a: The puja is timed to the midnight of the day when the eighth day of the waning moon, ashtami, is in force, ideally with Rohini star. Calculate it for your own location, not India's; a US panchangam or your local temple lists the nishita puja time. Families with small children often do the main puja earlier and a short prayer at midnight.

faq.q: When is Krishna Janmashtami celebrated?
faq.a: Janmashtami falls on the eighth day of the waning moon in Shravana or Bhadrapada, depending on the calendar your family follows, usually August or September. Smarta and Vaishnava communities sometimes observe it on consecutive days. Check the current year's panchangam for your region and your family's tradition.

## How do families keep Ganesh Chaturthi in the USA? — the fourth day of the bright half of Bhadrapada, usually August or September; bringing home a clay Ganesha; one-and-a-half, three, five or ten days depending on family custom and work schedules

## The home puja, on a Tuesday if need be — pranapratishta by a priest or a simple invocation, twenty-one blades of durva grass, kozhukattai or modak, a lamp at morning and evening; not looking at the moon that night, and the Syamantaka jewel story behind it

Close: Avvaiyar sang her Vinayagar Agaval to Ganesha; this week, keep him in mind at one doorway, the front door, every time you leave.
takeaways: In the USA, families bring home a clay Ganesha for Ganesh Chaturthi, keep a simple puja for one to ten days, and join temple celebrations on the nearest weekend.
Since most local waters are off limits for immersion, many dissolve the clay Ganesha at home in a bucket and pour the water into the garden.

faq.q: Where to buy clay Ganesha in the USA?
faq.a: Many Hindu temples in the US sell clay Ganesha images in the weeks before Chaturthi, and Indian grocery stores often stock them. Community groups hold workshops where families shape their own from natural clay. Look for unpainted or naturally coloured clay so it dissolves easily in water. Order or reserve early, because popular sizes sell out.

faq.q: How do I do a Ganesh Chaturthi celebration at home in the USA?
faq.a: Set up a clean platform with a cloth, place the clay Ganesha, and invoke him with a lamp, flowers, durva grass and a short prayer, or ask a priest to do pranapratishta. Offer modak or kozhukattai and fruit, do aarti morning and evening, and invite friends. After one and a half to ten days, do a farewell puja and immerse the image.

faq.q: Do US temples celebrate Ganesh Chaturthi?
faq.a: Yes. Ganesh Chaturthi at US temples usually brings abhishekam, special pujas, and often a multi-day festival, clay Ganesha workshops for children and a procession. Because the festival often falls on a weekday, the biggest community events usually take place on the nearest weekend. Check your local temple's schedule a few weeks ahead.

faq.q: Why shouldn't you look at the moon on Ganesh Chaturthi?
faq.a: The story says Ganesha, after a big meal of modak, tripped and his belly burst, and the moon laughed at him. Ganesha cursed that anyone seeing the moon on Chaturthi would face false accusation. Krishna himself, the Bhagavata Purana says, was falsely accused over the Syamantaka jewel. Hearing that story is the traditional remedy for an accidental glance.

outline: Hook: Visarjan means letting go. You can do it in a bucket on your back porch and lose nothing of the meaning; you may even understand it better, because you watch the whole return.

## How do you do visarjan at home in a bucket? — the uttara puja: a last aarti, akshata, modak and a sankalpam asking Ganesha to return; carrying him to a clean bucket of water, lowering him slowly, chanting 'Ganapati Bappa Morya'

## What to do with the water and the clay — letting it dissolve over a day or two, stirring gently, pouring the water into plants or a garden bed, keeping a pinch of clay for a pot; flowers go to compost

takeaways: An eco friendly Ganesh visarjan uses unbaked natural clay, a farewell puja at home, and a bucket of water in which the image dissolves over a day or two.

faq.q: How do you do Ganesh visarjan at home in a bucket?
faq.a: After the farewell puja, fill a clean bucket or tub with enough water to cover the image. Carry Ganesha to it with the family, say a short prayer asking him to return, and lower the image in gently. Leave it to dissolve, stirring now and then. Once the clay has settled, pour the water and clay into your garden or potted plants.

faq.q: How long does it take to dissolve clay Ganesha?
faq.a: An unbaked natural clay Ganesha usually softens within hours and dissolves fully in one to two days, depending on size and thickness. Stirring the water gently helps. Painted or baked images, and those made of plaster of Paris, may not dissolve at all, which is why natural clay is recommended. Remove any decorations before immersion.

faq.q: What are the Ganesh visarjan puja steps?
faq.a: The farewell, called uttara puja, begins with lighting the lamp and offering flowers, durva grass, akshata, modak and fruit. The family does a final aarti, asks forgiveness for any lapses, and moves the image slightly to signal departure. Then Ganesha is carried to the water with chanting and immersed. Some families tie a little curd rice in a cloth for his journey.

outline: Hook: Most stories about asuras end with a defeat. Onam's story ends with an asura king pushed into the underworld, and an entire people setting flowers at the door so he will feel welcome when he visits.

faq.a: The saptapadi mantras are short Sanskrit lines spoken as the groom leads the bride through each step. They ask Vishnu to walk with her for food, for strength, for wealth, for happiness, for children, for the seasons and for friendship. The final line, calling her his friend after seven steps, is often quoted as the heart of a Hindu marriage.

faq.q: What does sakha saptapadi bhava mean?
faq.a: It means 'be my friend, having taken seven steps with me'. The words close the saptapadi and treat friendship as the ground of the marriage. There is an old saying in Sanskrit that seven steps taken together make two people friends. So the ritual says that before roles or duties, the couple are companions who have chosen to walk together.

faq.q: Is saptapadi the most important part of a Hindu wedding?
faq.a: In many traditions, saptapadi is treated as the moment the marriage becomes complete, and the couple are called husband and wife only after the seventh step. Other rites carry deep meaning too, such as kanyadanam, tying the thali or mangalsutra, and walking around the fire. Communities weigh them differently, but the seven steps are nearly universal.

## Is patience the same as keeping quiet? — the Tirukkural's chapter on forbearance praises patience with others' faults, but patience is not silence about harm; seasons of strain versus situations that need protection

Close: one small thing to carry into this week: ask your spouse one question about their day and wait for the whole answer before you speak.
takeaways: Prayer for marriage problems works best as steadying your own mind and heart, not as a way to change your spouse; pray for the marriage, not against a person.
Prayer sits alongside real help such as counselling; where there is abuse or fear, safety and professional support come first.

faq.q: Is there a mantra for peace between husband and wife?
faq.a: Many families chant 'Om Uma Maheshwarabhyam Namaha', honouring Shiva and Parvati as the ideal couple, or the Ardhanarishvara Stotram, which praises the half-male, half-female form. Chanting it together, or alone at a lamp, can soften the mood of a home. Tradition offers it as support for patience and understanding, alongside honest conversation, not as a replacement for it.

faq.q: What is the Hindu view of marriage problems?
faq.a: Hindu tradition sees marriage as a shared dharma, a path two people walk through changing seasons, and its stories do not hide conflict. Shiva and Parvati quarrel, separate and return. The emphasis falls on patience, forgiveness and mutual respect. Tradition does not ask anyone to endure harm; seeking counsel from elders or professionals is consistent with it.

faq.q: How do I pray when my marriage is struggling?

## What is mangalsutra meaning, word by word? — mangala, auspicious, and sutra, thread; the thali in Tamil homes, minnu in Kerala, black beads in Maharashtra and the North; a pendant that differs by community and family deity

## Why three knots? — moondru mudichu: explanations vary, from body, speech and mind to the three worlds or the couple's three commitments; the Mangalya Dharanam mantra asking for a long life together

## Renewing the thread — the manjal kayiru replaced on Aadi Perukku, Karadaiyan Nombu and the Meenakshi Thirukalyanam day; changing to gold chain after the wedding; the story is really about a promise that needs retying

Close: a gentle reframe: a thread is the weakest material a promise could be made of, which is exactly why it has to be looked after. Many women today choose how and when to wear it, and the meaning survives.
takeaways: Mangalsutra means auspicious thread; in Tamil homes it is the thali, tied with three knots during the wedding as the couple's promise to each other.
Designs differ by region and community, and the turmeric thread is renewed on festivals such as Aadi Perukku, a sign that the promise is kept alive.

faq.q: What is the thali meaning in a Tamil wedding?
faq.a: In a Tamil wedding the thali is a gold pendant on a turmeric-dyed thread, tied around the bride's neck by the groom at the muhurtham, the auspicious moment, while drums and nadaswaram play. Its design often reflects the family's community or deity. It marks the marriage and carries blessings for the couple's long and happy life together.

faq.q: What do the three knots in a mangalsutra mean?
faq.a: Explanations of the three knots in a mangalsutra vary. Some families say they stand for the bride's commitment in mind, speech and action; others link them to the three worlds, or to husband, wife and their families. In many Tamil weddings the groom ties the first knot and his sister ties the other two, drawing the family into the promise.

faq.q: What does the mangalya dharanam mantra mean?
faq.a: The mantra chanted as the thali is tied, beginning 'Mangalyam tantunanena', says in essence: this is the sacred thread, essential for my life; I tie it around your neck, O auspicious one; may you live happily for a hundred years. It is a blessing for a long, shared life, spoken as the promise is made visible.

faq.q: Why is the mangalsutra thread changed on Aadi Perukku?
faq.a: On Aadi Perukku, and on days like Karadaiyan Nombu and the Meenakshi Thirukalyanam, many Tamil married women replace the turmeric thread holding the thali with a fresh one. It is a small act of renewal tied to seasons of prayer for the household. Families differ; some move the thali to a gold chain after the first year.

faq.q: Is there a Shiva Parvati prayer for couples?

faq.q: What is a simple daily prayer for husband and wife?

## What is Thalai Deepavali? — a Tamil custom: the couple's first Deepavali, hosted by the bride's family; new clothes for both, gifts for the son-in-law, the pre-dawn celebration, sweets and the first firecrackers together; Deepavali falls around the new moon of Aippasi, usually October or November

takeaways: Thalai Deepavali is a newlywed couple's first Deepavali, traditionally spent at the bride's parents' home with new clothes, gifts for the son-in-law and a pre-dawn celebration.

faq.q: What are the usual Thalai Deepavali gifts for son in law?
faq.a: Common thalai deepavali gifts for son in law include a silk veshti and shirt, a gold ring or chain, and sometimes silver vessels or a watch; the bride receives a silk sari and jewellery. Customs vary widely by family and community, and many families today keep gifts modest. The gifts are a gesture of welcome and affection, not an obligation.

faq.q: What should a couple do on their first Diwali after marriage?
faq.a: On the first Diwali after marriage, Tamil couples traditionally visit the bride's parents, wear new clothes they gift, take the early-morning oil bath, pray together, and seek elders' blessings before sweets and crackers. In other regions, the couple may spend it with the groom's family. Whatever the custom, praying together and honouring both families is the heart of it.

faq.q: How can we celebrate Thalai Deepavali in the USA?
faq.a: If you cannot travel, keep the core: wear new clothes, ideally ones sent by the bride's parents, light a lamp together before dawn, and do a short Lakshmi or Ganesha prayer. Time a video call to India's morning so parents can bless you. Cook one dish from each family, invite friends in the evening, and plan a visit home when you can.
